paragraphs: Rabbi Shasha, son of Rabbi Abba. (Sheshai; Ezra.)[^1]

He is mentioned at the beginning of Shemot Rabbah, chapter 24: he would write the he below and the lamed above, in the word הלה׳ in the phrase “Is this how you repay the Lord?” Yuḥasin has the reading “bar Rava.” But the source of the midrash is the Yerushalmi, Megillah, chapter 1, halakhah 9, where the reading is “Rabbi Yosha, son of Rav Chanael.” The Yerushalmi’s reading is the correct one, as Rav Chanael too is known to have been a scribe.[^2]

notes.text: The heading reads ששא, not ששת (Sheshet); Shasha is a transliteration of that unpointed spelling, not a claim to have established its vocalization. Hyman’s parenthesis reads ששי, עזרא פ״ד־כ. Sheshai represents ששי; the Ezra locator is kept here exactly as printed because its intended reference is unresolved.

רפ״כד means the beginning of chapter 24, rather than its end; ש״ר is rendered by the customary title Shemot Rabbah. The names יושע׳ and חנאל are kept distinct from the earlier English normalizations Yehoshua and Chananel. The Yuḥasin variant is printed בר רבא, rendered bar Rava. The relative positions of the letters, the preference for the Yerushalmi reading and the assertion that Chanael was a scribe are Hyman’s statements; no cited edition or underlying passage was independently checked. The quoted Hebrew phrase is הלה׳ תגמלו זאת. The printed Yerushalmi locator is ה״ט־יא :; it is retained here exactly, without treating it as a range of halakhot or assigning a verified modern locus.
